name: Common Pochard
rangeDescription: Palearctic, breeding british isles and southern scandinavia eastward through east-central russia, in south from iberian peninsula and türkiye eastward through northeastern china; winters to tropical africa and india eastward to japan and southward to the northern philippines
description: Mid-sized diving duck. Male distinctive, with dark rusty head, pale gray body contrasting with black breast, and broad pale bluish band on bill.

name: Angola Waxbill
rangeDescription: Angola and namibia
description: A tiny colorful seed-eating waxbill with a grayish breast, a yellow belly, an olive-green back finely barred with dark gray, and a scarlet rump and upper tail. The male has a black throat patch that the female lacks.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Gray-headed Elaenia
rangeDescription: Southeastern peru, northern bolivia, and adjacent brazil (undescribed subspecies, not true caniceps?); eastern and southern bolivia southward to northwestern argentina and eastward to paraguay, northeastern argentina, and south-central and eastern brazil
description: Small flycatcher found in humid forest in lowlands and lower mountain slopes. Male is gray with paler underparts and dark wings with white wingbars.

name: White-bellied Nothura
rangeDescription: Northeastern brazil to eastern bolivia and northeastern paraguay
description: Small, sand-colored tinamou with a mix of rusty and dark spots on the back and a white belly. Found in natural and human-modified grasslands, where it is difficult to catch sight of due to its retiring nature and cryptic plumage.

name: Fiji Woodswallow
rangeDescription: Northern fiji (yasawa and viti levu to taveuni and qamea)
description: A thick-bodied, highly aerobatic bird, white below and dark above with a dark chin and white cheek. Often perches on wires.

name: North Island Kokako
rangeDescription: North and great barrier islands (new zealand)
description: Large songbird confined to a few scattered forests in the northern half of the North Island of New Zealand, and some offshore island sanctuaries where predator control is undertaken. Adults have a slate blue-gray body with vibrant cerulean wattles and a distinct black mask.

name: Pemba Sunbird
rangeDescription: Pemba island (off northeastern tanzania)
description: Male is iridescent green above and dark below, with a purple band across the breast. Female is nondescript, with a pale eyebrow and blurry streaking across the pale yellowish underparts.

name: Island Scrub-Jay
rangeDescription: Santa cruz island (channel islands off southern california)
description: The largest and darkest scrub-jay, identifiable solely based on range: found exclusively on Santa Cruz Island off southern California. Similar to California Scrub-Jay but larger, with darker back and darker mask.

name: Uniform Finch
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Slender finch found at forest borders where it is especially associated with bamboo. Usually forages on or near the ground.

name: Alagoas Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Highlands of northeastern brazil (alagoas)
description: Small flycatcher with a long tail, which is often held cocked. Has an olive back and whitish underparts.

name: Red-bearded Bee-eater
rangeDescription: Malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Unmistakable leaf-green bee-eater of lowland and foothill forests. Namesake “beard” actually goes from the crown all the way down to the belly.

name: Little Cormorant
rangeDescription: Lowlands of india to southeastern asia and northern java
description: An all black ducklike waterbird with a distinctive flattish head and a bill that is sharply hooked at the tip. Smallest of the cormorants found in the region.

name: Black-spectacled Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (ayacucho and huancavelica)
description: Rare brushfinch with a highly restricted range in the eastern Andes of central Peru. It has an ornate head pattern with a partial black mask bordered by chestnut, black-and-white mustache stripes, and a white spot between the eye and the bill.

name: Damara Red-billed Hornbill
rangeDescription: Central namibia (southern damaraland)
description: Fairly small, slim, long-tailed hornbill. Note the red bill, dark eye, pale face, and heavily spotted back.

name: Akohekohe
rangeDescription: Ohia forest of eastern maui; formerly on molokai
description: A large, rare Hawaiian Honeycreeper of high elevation wet forests on eastern Maui. Its bushy, forward-pointing crest is distinctive.

name: Long-tailed Glossy Starling
rangeDescription: Far southern mauritania to northern guinea eastward to southern sudan and northwestern south sudan
description: A large, extremely long-tailed, dark and glossy starling. Sometimes looks black, but in good light shows iridescence that is mostly blue-green, with a purple belly and tail.

name: White-striped Warbler
rangeDescription: Gallery forest of south-central brazil
description: Hyperactive warbler that nervously and continually flicks its tail in the understory of forests near water. Note the broad white eyebrow fringed with gray and the narrow dark mask.
imageCreditName: João Vitor Andriola | Brazil Birding Experts

name: Fiery-browed Myna
rangeDescription: Mountains of sulawesi
description: An unmistakable, long-tailed, conspicuous myna with a broad orange eyebrow, a pale eye, an ash-gray body, mossy green wings and tail, and a contrasting yellowish rump. Juvenile browner, with a narrower eyebrow and a dark eye.

name: Hooded Berryeater
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (espírito santo to rio grande do sul)
description: Big and chunky rainforest cotinga with a long tail. Found in the canopy of montane forests where it can be locally common, but hard to see.

name: Gray Peacock-Pheasant
rangeDescription: Northeastern india and bhutan eastward to far southern china, southward to the base of the thai-malay peninsula, central laos, and central vietnam
description: A strange-looking pheasant which passes ghostlike through dense forests, seldom venturing into the open. Both sexes are gray-brown with iridescent spotting on the wings, but the male has a longer tail and a bushy, forward-arching crest.
